When you first gain the Air sphere, gain proficiency in one of the following skills: Acrobatics, Athletics, Perception, Performance, or Survival.
If you already have proficiency in the chosen skill, choose one Mortal Realm Air talent instead.
You also learn Gather Current and Wind Lash.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":672,"source_global_line_start":669,"source_heading":"Wind-Hand Training","source_local_line_end":103,"source_local_line_start":100,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Gather Current","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Gather Current
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
Cost: None
You stir a small controlled Air Current in a 10-foot cube you can see within range.
When you create the Current, choose one Vector:
Lift: A willing creature that starts in or enters the Current before it ends may add 5 feet to one jump or ignore the first 10 feet of falling damage before the Current ends.
Press: The first hostile creature that starts in or enters the Current before it ends treats the Current’s space as Difficult Terrain.
Scatter: Nonmagical smoke, loose dust, harmless vapor, light fog, or similar airborne material in the Current is dispersed or shifted 10 feet.
Carry: A whisper, scent, ribbon, Tiny unattended object weighing no more than 1 pound, or comparable harmless sign may be carried from one point in the Current to another point in the Current.
Turn: The first ordinary Tiny projectile that passes through the Current before it ends has Disadvantage on its attack roll.

Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row

Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. On a hit, the target takes bludgeoning or slashing damage equal to 1d8 + your Path key ability modifier.
The damage increases by 1d8 at CL 5, CL 11, and CL 17.
When Wind Lash hits, choose one basic Vector:
Push: Push the target 5 feet directly away from you if it is no more than one size larger than you.
Pull: Pull the target 5 feet directly toward you if it is no more than one size larger than you.
Cut: The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
Lift: The target’s next jump before the start of your next turn is increased by 5 feet if the target is willing. If the target is unwilling, this option has no effect.

Choose one Field Formula you know and resolve its effect. You know the following Field Formulae when you learn Alchemy:
#### Medicinal Smoke
Choose yourself or one ally within range.

#### Corrosive Dregs

Proficiency Bonus + Alchemy key ability modifier, minimum 1

Gain Tame.
##### Tame
Train one non-sapient Beast to obey commands in and out of combat.
Requirements:
find, purchase, rescue, raise, or capture the creature;
spend 8 hours training one creature;
make a Wisdom (Animal Handling) check. The DC is:
10 + the creature’s Challenge Rating
Successful Check: The creature becomes Tame.
Failed Check: The creature is not Tame. You may train again after addressing an appropriate narrative obstacle.
You may train only one creature at a time.
##### Tamer Capacity
You may maintain:
a number of Tame Creatures no greater than your Proficiency Bonus;
a total combined Challenge Rating no greater than the table. After the first CR 0 creature, treat each additional CR 0 creature as CR 1/8.

##### Commands
Tame Creatures follow your commands to the best of their ability.
Giving ordinary commands requires no Action unless a talent says otherwise.
Without a command, a Tame Creature acts according to its nature, training, and circumstances.

When another creature attempts to control one of your Tame Creatures, it must first make:
Charisma check
opposed by your:
Wisdom (Animal Handling) check
Failed Opposed Check: The control attempt fails.
Successful Opposed Check: Resolve the controlling effect normally.
##### Awakening
A beast that becomes sapient is no longer an ordinary Tame Creature.
Its future relationship should be resolved through:
consent;
narrative agreement;
a Beast Companion bond;
Beast-sphere cultivation;
Spirit practices;
or another appropriate feature. gain Smith’s Tools proficiency or one alternate artisan’s tool proficiency as described above;

[{"component_name":"Grave Sense","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Grave Sense
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No action; you may focus as an Action for more detail
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Range: 30 feet
Cost: None
You can sense strong nearby death-signs.
You can detect the presence and direction, but not exact identity, of the following within range:
corpses;
undead;
dying creatures at 0 HP;
ghosts or lingering death echoes;
grave Qi;
recent violent death;
active Death sphere effects.
As an Action, you may focus on one death-sign you can sense and learn one of the following:
whether it is corpse, undead, ghost, dying creature, grave Qi, or active Death effect;
whether the death was recent or old;
whether a corpse has been preserved, desecrated, animated, or protected by a rite;
whether an undead creature appears bound, feral, willing, commanded, or self-willed;
whether a possession or soul-binding effect is present, if it is visible to Death Sense.
Grave Sense does not automatically reveal hidden creatures, invisible creatures, a complete stat block, the target’s Path, the target’s Realm, or private memories.
At CL 10, the range becomes 60 feet. AC: 10 + your Proficiency Bonus
HP: 3 x your CL + your key ability modifier
Speed: 25 feet
Damage Immunities: Poison
Condition Immunities: Charmed, Frightened, Poisoned
Senses: passive Perception 8 + your Proficiency Bonus
Languages: understands your commands; cannot speak unless a feature says otherwise
Grave Strike: Melee attack using your Cultivation Attack Modifier, reach 5 feet, one target.

Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: Ritual
Time: 10 minutes
Range: Touch
Target: One Common corpse or suitable set of remains
Duration: 8 hours, or until the servant is destroyed or dismissed
Cost: 1 CP
Control Load: 1
Requirement: You must have enough unused Death Control Limit to maintain the servant, and the target must be a legal corpse under the Corpse Availability rules.
You animate the target with grave Qi as one Lesser Corpse Servant. It appears in the corpse's space with full Hit Points and uses the Lesser Corpse Servant stat block below.
The servant is one undead asset. It counts against your Death Control Limit, acts immediately after your turn, and is commanded according to Commanding Death Servants. If it is not commanded, it takes the Dodge action and moves only as permitted by those rules.
A Lesser Corpse Servant does not contain the original soul unless another talent says so. It can follow simple commands, perform labor, carry objects, open doors, keep watch, pull carts, dig, clean, guard a threshold, or fight if commanded.
You may maintain only one Lesser Corpse Servant created by this base ability at a time. You may dismiss that servant without taking an action on your turn. If you complete this ritual while one of your Lesser Corpse Servants from this ability still exists, the earlier servant must be dismissed before the new one is created.

[{"component_name":"Diagnose the Sickness","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Diagnose the Sickness
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Touch, or 30 feet if you can clearly perceive the target
Target: One creature, corpse, object, patch of terrain, sample, wound, room, or obvious contamination source

Cost: None
You read the signs of disease and hostile biological or spiritual patterns.
You learn whether Disease is present and one of the following facts:
whether the infection is ordinary, magical, spiritual, alchemical, demonic, or unknown;
whether the target carries any of your Contagion Tokens;
whether the target is Sickened;
whether the infection appears contagious in the current scene;
whether the condition is worsening;
whether ordinary medicine might help;
whether quarantine is recommended;
whether the target is an active carrier, passive carrier, or merely contaminated.

Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action

Range: 60 feet
Area: 10-foot-radius sphere

Cost: 2 CP
You raise a visible or invisible veil of quarantine marks, medicinal smoke, spirit fever, miasma threads, salt circles, bone needles, paper seals, humming insects, or coughing ghosts.
When you create the veil, choose one mode: Containment or Outbreak.
##### Containment Mode
Choose any number of creatures in the area.
Chosen creatures gain Advantage on saving throws against Disease while they remain inside the veil.
Whenever a chosen creature starts its turn inside the veil, it may remove one Contagion Token from itself.
Disease effects created by you cannot spread from inside the veil to creatures outside the veil unless you allow it.
##### Outbreak Mode
When an enemy enters the area for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there, it must make a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature takes 1d6 Necrotic, Poison, or Psychic damage and becomes Sickened until the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: The creature takes half damage and is not Sickened.

Factory Combat Bucket: reaction

Cost: None
Use Limit: Once per round
You receive an incoming force and decide where it continues.
You may use Flowing Response when one of the following triggers occurs:
a creature you can see makes a melee attack roll against you;
a creature within your reach attempts to Grapple or Shove you;
a creature within your reach forces you to make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw to avoid being moved, knocked Prone, Grappled, or Restrained.
Choose the matching response.
##### Yield Against an Attack
Increase your AC against the triggering melee attack by your Proficiency Bonus.

Gain Advantage on the triggering saving throw against the Grapple, Shove, forced movement, Prone effect, or Restrained effect.

You cultivate the art of becoming the enemy’s most immediate problem.

it has Disadvantage on attack rolls that do not include you as a target;
it has Advantage on attack rolls targeting only you;
if it cannot legally perceive, reach, or target you, it does not suffer Disadvantage merely because it attacks another creature;
when you successfully Challenge another creature, your previous Challenge ends unless a talent says otherwise.

You cultivate the art of deciding which ground an enemy may cross only by answering you.
#### Patrol
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Duration: Until the start of your next turn
Cost: None
Establish a Patrol Zone centered on yourself.
The Patrol Zone extends a distance equal to:
your melee reach + 10 feet
When a hostile creature you can perceive moves into, out of, or through your Patrol Zone, you may make one Patrol Response.
#### Patrol Response
A Patrol Response allows you to:
move up to your remaining Patrol Movement into a legal space that brings the triggering creature within your melee reach;
make one opportunity attack against that creature.
The first Patrol Response you make before the start of your next turn requires your Reaction.
At higher Cultivation Levels, you gain additional Patrol Responses each round that do not require your Reaction:
| Cultivation Level | Additional Patrol Responses |
| --- | --- |
| 1-4 | 0 |
| 5-10 | 1 |
| 11-16 | 2 |
| 17-20 | 3 |

These additional Patrol Responses:
may be used only while Patrol remains active;
are still treated as Reactions for rules that limit one response to one trigger;
cannot trigger another Reaction talent from the same triggering movement;
do not restore your ordinary Reaction;
cannot be used more than once during the same creature’s turn.
#### Patrol Movement
When you establish Patrol, your total Patrol Movement before the start of your next turn equals your Speed.
Movement spent through Patrol Responses:
reduces your remaining Patrol Movement;
follows a legal route;
provokes opportunity attacks normally;
cannot exceed your remaining Patrol Movement;
does not reduce your Speed during your own turn.
#### Patrol Attack Limits
A Patrol attack:
is an opportunity attack;
may be made only once per triggering creature’s turn;
cannot trigger itself;
does not deal Sneak Attack damage or comparable precision damage unless a talent explicitly permits it;
still requires a legal melee attack and a weapon, unarmed strike, or natural weapon able to reach the target.
#### Zone Talent Limit

You gain training in the basic language of living patterns.
You can recognize obvious signs of bleeding, suffocation, poisoning, disease, dying, shock, spiritual drift, and broken meridian flow. This does not replace a Medicine check, Alchemy diagnosis, or Spirit Awakening perception when the cause is hidden.

Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action

Duration: Instantaneous

You read the target’s living pattern.

You may place a Pulse Seal on the target.
If you use Read the Pulse as an Action instead of a Bonus Action, you also learn the general nature of one disease, poison, injury, or condition affecting the target. The GM may describe this in practical terms rather than revealing hidden stat-block names.
You may use Read the Pulse on a corpse that has been dead no longer than 1 day. If you do, you learn the most obvious cause of death.
You may use Read the Pulse on a creature bearing your Pulse Seal regardless of distance or line of effect, provided the creature is on the same plane of existence. When you do, you know the creature’s direction and distance from you.

[{"component_name":"Appraise the Venom","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Appraise the Venom
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Touch, or 30 feet if you can clearly perceive the target
Target: One creature, corpse, object, wound, food, drink, weapon, sample, patch of terrain, or visible contamination source
Duration: Instantaneous
Cost: None
You read toxic traces, venom patterns, corrosion, and poisonous residue.
You learn whether poison is present and one of the following facts:
whether the poison is ordinary, alchemical, spiritual, demonic, plant-based, beast-based, mineral, corrosive, or unknown;
whether the target is Poisoned;
whether the target carries any of your Dose Marks;
whether the target has Toxin Burden;
whether the target suffers an Ingrained Toxin;
whether the poison appears immediately dangerous, delayed, or long-term;
whether an ordinary antidote might help;
whether the poison can be safely handled in the current scene;
whether the poison appears connected to Alchemy, Disease, Blood, Flowers, Death, or another sphere.
When you use Appraise the Venom on a poison, a poisoned target, or a sample, you may create an Antidote Profile for it.
If you spend 1 CP when using Appraise the Venom, learn three facts instead of one.
Appraise the Venom does not automatically reveal exact formulas, hidden creators, secret techniques, rare antidote recipes, or the full history of a toxin.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":60777,"source_global_line_start":60756,"source_heading":"Appraise the Venom","source_local_line_end":150,"source_local_line_start":129,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Action","cost":"None","duration":"Instantaneous","factory_combat_bucket":"action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"Touch, or 30 feet if you can clearly perceive the target","target":"One creature, corpse, object, wound, food, drink, weapon, sample, patch of terrain, or visible contamination source"}},{"component_name":"Deliver the Dose","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Deliver the Dose
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet, or weapon range if delivered through a weapon
Target: One creature or object
Duration: Instantaneous
Cost: None
You deliver venom, toxic qi, corrosive fluid, a poisoned needle, mineral dust, spirit spores, toxic breath, or a coated strike.
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack. If you deliver the dose through a weapon attack, make the weapon attack normally instead.
On a hit, the target takes Poison or Acid damage, chosen when you attack.
Mortal: 1d8Foundation: 2d8Core Formation: 3d8Nascent Soul: 4d8
Once per turn when you hit a creature with Deliver the Dose, the target makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The target gains 1 Dose Mark and has Disadvantage on its next ability check before the start of your next turn.
Successful Save: The target does not gain a Dose Mark.
Deliver the Dose cannot place Dose Marks on creatures immune to the delivery method, damage type, or Poison sphere effect used.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":60793,"source_global_line_start":60778,"source_heading":"Deliver the Dose","source_local_line_end":166,"source_local_line_start":151,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Action","cost":"None","duration":"Instantaneous","factory_combat_bucket":"action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"60 feet, or weapon range if delivered through a weapon","target":"One creature or object"}},{"component_name":"Ingrain the Toxin","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Ingrain the Toxin
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 60 feet, or touch for Body Refining use
Target: One creature with at least 2 Dose Marks from you
Duration: Until the target finishes a long rest or receives treatment
Cost: 2 CP
You spend 2 Dose Marks on the target and attempt to lodge a minor lingering toxin into the body, meridian flow, breath, or spirit.
The target makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: Choose one Minor Ingrained Toxin effect:
Bitter Breath. The target has Disadvantage on its next Constitution saving throw before its next long rest.
Numb Channels. The target’s Speed is reduced by 5 feet until its next long rest.
Sour Blood. The next healing the target receives before its next long rest is reduced by your Proficiency Bonus.
Clouded Senses. The target has Disadvantage on its next Wisdom (Perception) check before its next long rest.
Heavy Pulse. The target cannot benefit from the Dash action on its next turn, and has Disadvantage on its next Dexterity saving throw before its next long rest.
Successful Save: The Dose Marks are spent, but no Ingrained Toxin takes hold.
A Minor Ingrained Toxin is intentionally limited. Serious long-term poison requires Foundation, Core Formation, or Nascent Soul talents.
A creature can identify or treat a Minor Ingrained Toxin with appropriate Medicine, Alchemy, Life, Poison, or purification methods. The treatment DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":60812,"source_global_line_start":60794,"source_heading":"Ingrain the Toxin","source_local_line_end":185,"source_local_line_start":167,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Action","cost":"2 CP","duration":"Until the target finishes a long rest or receives treatment","factory_combat_bucket":"action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"60 feet, or touch for Body Refining use","target":"One creature with at least 2 Dose Marks from you"}}]

[{"component_name":"Aegis","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Aegis
An Aegis is a protective cultivation effect placed on one creature.
Unless a talent says otherwise:
A creature may benefit from only one Aegis created by the same cultivator at a time.
An Aegis uses Concentration unless made Persistent.
An Aegis may be ended early by its creator without spending an action.
An unwilling creature may make a Wisdom saving throw to resist receiving an Aegis. Aegis talents replace the Armored Aegis unless the talent explicitly says it augments another Aegis.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":63286,"source_global_line_start":63280,"source_heading":"Aegis","source_local_line_end":19,"source_local_line_start":13,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Armored Aegis","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Armored Aegis
When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Aegis talent automatically.
Protective barriers wrap the target.
The target’s base AC becomes equal to your Cultivation Save DC.
The target does not add its Dexterity modifier to this AC.
Armored Aegis does not stack with worn armor, but the target may still benefit from a shield.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":63328,"source_global_line_start":63323,"source_heading":"Armored Aegis","source_local_line_end":61,"source_local_line_start":56,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Succor","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Succor
A Succor is a sacrificial rescue. The base Protection sphere does not grant a Succor effect automatically; Succor talents provide the triggers and effects.
To use Succor, a trigger stated by one Succor talent you know must occur and that talent must have an eligible target. The target must currently benefit from one of your Persistent Aegises. The detailed Reaction procedure appears under the base Succor ability below.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":63289,"source_global_line_start":63287,"source_heading":"Succor","source_local_line_end":22,"source_local_line_start":20,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Ward","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Ward
A Ward is a temporary protected area.
Unless a talent says otherwise:
a Ward is centered within range;
a Ward remains where it was created;
a Ward uses Concentration unless made Persistent;
you may reduce its size when creating it;
you may maintain only one Ward at a time. Ward talents replace Barrier Ward unless the talent explicitly modifies Barrier Ward.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":63297,"source_global_line_start":63290,"source_heading":"Ward","source_local_line_end":30,"source_local_line_start":23,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Barrier Ward","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Barrier Ward
When you learn the Protection sphere, you learn this Ward talent automatically.
Create a mostly transparent wall along the Ward’s perimeter.
The Barrier blocks:
movement through its edge;
attacks crossing its edge;
breath weapons crossing its edge;
destructive blasts crossing its edge;
ghost strikes crossing its edge;
other effects that must physically travel to their destination. The Barrier does not automatically block teleportation, mind-affecting effects, gaze attacks, or abilities that do not travel through the wall.
##### Barrier Placement
If the Barrier cuts through a creature’s space when it appears, the creature chooses one side and is pushed into the nearest legal space on that side.
If the Barrier and another solid surface would completely enclose a creature, it may make a Dexterity saving throw.
Successful Save: The creature may use its Reaction to move up to its Speed into the nearest legal space outside the enclosure.
Failed Save: The creature remains enclosed.
The Barrier extends into the Ethereal Plane.
##### Barrier Statistics
If the Barrier reaches 0 HP, the Ward ends.
##### Overflow Damage
If an attack deals more damage than the Barrier’s current HP, the attacker may burst through.
Subtract the Barrier’s remaining HP from the attack’s damage.
If the attack can legally continue to a creature on the other side, make a new attack roll against one target within range.
On a hit, deal the remaining damage.
Area damage that bursts through affects creatures on the other side with its remaining damage.
##### Crushing Through
A creature may use an Action to attempt to shove or overrun the Barrier.
Make a Strength (Athletics) check against your Cultivation Save DC.
Successful Check: The Barrier shatters and the Ward ends.
Failed Check: The Barrier remains.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":63383,"source_global_line_start":63355,"source_heading":"Barrier Ward","source_local_line_end":116,"source_local_line_start":88,"structured_fields":{}}]

gain proficiency with Woodcarver’s Tools, Weaver’s Tools, Smith’s Tools, Tinker’s Tools, Calligrapher’s Supplies, or Sleight of Hand;
if already proficient with your chosen option, choose one Puppetry talent for which you meet the prerequisites as a bonus talent;

The vessel cannot fly, swim, burrow, squeeze through impossible spaces, or climb smooth surfaces unless a talent, construction, or feature allows it.

[{"component_name":"Apply Modulation","exact_source_excerpt":"##### Apply Modulation
Once per turn, when you activate a sphere technique you know, you may apply one Modulation talent you know to that technique and pay the listed cost.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":65644,"source_global_line_start":65643,"source_heading":"Apply Modulation","source_local_line_end":190,"source_local_line_start":189,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Minor Qi Arts","exact_source_excerpt":"##### Minor Qi Arts
You learn to perform harmless adjustments to ambient Qi.
As an Action, you may create one minor effect within 30 feet:
color, warm, chill, flavor, clean, or soil a Tiny object;
cause a faint harmless sound, scent, breeze, spark, ripple, or glow;
make a small symbol, seal, footprint, or line of script appear for 1 minute;
open or close an unlocked Tiny mundane object such as a pouch clasp or paper fan;
predict ordinary weather signs for the next hour when outdoors;
cause a candle, incense stick, lamp wick, or similar tiny flame to brighten, dim, or extinguish.
Minor Qi Arts cannot deal damage, impose a condition, create Cover, duplicate another sphere talent, activate a magic item, or deceive a careful observer by itself.
If your table uses spell cantrips directly, the GM may allow Minor Qi Arts to count as druidcraft, prestidigitation, and thaumaturgy for prerequisite and harmless utility purposes. Use your Key Ability as the spellcasting ability for such cantrips.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":65642,"source_global_line_start":65632,"source_heading":"Minor Qi Arts","source_local_line_end":188,"source_local_line_start":178,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Qi Bond","exact_source_excerpt":"##### Qi Bond
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, object, or Active Qi Pattern
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
Attempt to form a thread between your circulation and the target’s Qi pattern.
A willing creature, an unattended object, or an Active Qi Pattern you created is bonded automatically.
Against an unwilling creature, attended object, or hostile Active Qi Pattern, make a ranged Cultivation Attack. If the target is an Active Qi Pattern, treat its AC as equal to its creator’s Cultivation Save DC. If the creator is unknown, use 10 + Pattern Rank.
Hit: Create a Qi Bond.
Miss: No bond forms.
While the bond lasts, you may use your Action on each of your turns to apply one Bond talent you know to the target.
Unless a Bond talent says otherwise, the Qi Bond ends if:
the target is ever outside your Qi Bond range;
the target has Total Cover from you;
you use your Action for anything other than applying or maintaining a Bond talent;
you lose Concentration.
###### Persistent Qi Bond
Augment - 2 CP: The Qi Bond persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the bond on your turn without spending an Action.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":65628,"source_global_line_start":65606,"source_heading":"Qi Bond","source_local_line_end":174,"source_local_line_start":152,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Bonus Action","cost":"None","duration":"Concentration, up to 1 minute","factory_combat_bucket":"bonus_action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"30 feet","target":"One creature, object, or Active Qi Pattern"}},{"component_name":"Turbulent Field","exact_source_excerpt":"##### Turbulent Field
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Action
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: Self
Area: 5-foot-radius Emanation
Duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute
Cost: None
You emit a field of unstable Qi.
If the campaign uses wild magic or Qi-deviation rules, increase the instability chance of creatures inside the area by 50 percent.
If the campaign does not use a separate instability system, use the following fallback.
The first time on a turn that a creature inside the area activates a technique that costs CP or casts a spell using a spell slot, it makes a Constitution saving throw.
Failed Save: The technique is Turbulent until it resolves. A Turbulent technique suffers one complication chosen by the GM or rolled from a campaign-appropriate table, such as visible backlash, noisy activation, reduced range, accidental self-exposure, or minor damage to an unattended nearby object.
The fallback complication should be inconvenient but should not normally waste the technique unless another Turbulence talent says so.
The area radius increases by Realm:
Cultivation Level: 1-4 - Radius: 5 feet
Cultivation Level: 5-10 - Radius: 10 feet
Cultivation Level: 11-16 - Radius: 15 feet
Cultivation Level: 17-20 - Radius: 20 feet
###### Lingering Turbulence
Augment - 2 CP: The Turbulent Field persists for its remaining duration without Concentration.
You may apply this augment after creating the field on your turn without spending an Action.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":65676,"source_global_line_start":65654,"source_heading":"Turbulent Field","source_local_line_end":222,"source_local_line_start":200,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Action","area":"5-foot-radius Emanation","cost":"None","duration":"Concentration, up to 1 minute","factory_combat_bucket":"action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"Self"}},{"component_name":"Unweave Pattern","exact_source_excerpt":"##### Unweave Pattern
Classification: Base Qiweaving Ability
Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Canonical Action Type: Ritual Procedure
Factory Routing: procedure_ledger_not_combat_action
Timing Detail: 10 minutes
Range: 30 feet
Target: One creature, object, location, or Active Qi Pattern
Duration: Instantaneous
Cost: None
Attempt to end one Active Qi Pattern on the target.
If the pattern’s Pattern Rank is equal to or lower than half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down, it ends automatically.
Otherwise, make a Qiweaving Check against the pattern.
Successful Check: The pattern ends.
Failed Check: The pattern remains.
Unweave Pattern cannot end a Domain, Secret Inheritance, Formation project, artifact-level effect, or campaign-scale working unless a talent, project, or GM ruling explicitly permits it.
###### Rapid Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: Reduce the Action Type to Action.
If you Ready this Action to disrupt a technique as it is activated, resolve Unweave Pattern when the triggering technique is being created. On a successful check, the technique fails and any Action, CP, spell slot, or limited use spent on it is lost.
###### Broad Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: Attempt to unweave a number of additional Active Qi Patterns on the same target equal to half your Proficiency Bonus, rounded down.
Make a separate Qiweaving Check for each pattern that is not ended automatically.
###### Certain Unweave
Augment - 1 CP: The automatic-ending threshold becomes your Proficiency Bonus instead of half your Proficiency Bonus.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":65602,"source_global_line_start":65579,"source_heading":"Unweave Pattern","source_local_line_end":148,"source_local_line_start":125,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Ritual Procedure","canonical_action_type":"Ritual Procedure","cost":"None","duration":"Instantaneous","factory_routing":"procedure_ledger_not_combat_action","range":"30 feet","target":"One creature, object, location, or Active Qi Pattern","timing_detail":"10 minutes"}}]

[{"component_name":"Spool and Strand","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Base Ability - Spool and Strand
Action Type: Special Trigger
Canonical Action Type: Special Trigger
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Timing Detail: No action for ordinary handling; part of the action for Thread talents
Factory Routing: triggered_passive_modifier_row
Range: Self.
Cost: None for mundane thread; 1 CP to create or reinforce Qi Thread for combat use.
Effect: You can prepare, draw, control, and conceal combat-ready strands. You may use mundane thread, silk, wire, cord, needles, and hooks as thread tools. If you spend 1 CP, you can create Qi Thread from your fingertips, breath, weapon, sleeve, hair, blood, or dantian pressure for 1 minute.
Ordinary Uses: You can sew, bind, stitch, tie knots, mend cloth, mark a path with thread, set a simple cord, prepare a hidden sleeve spool, or handle fine threadwork without a check unless the situation is difficult.
Combat Use: Spool and Strand enables your Thread talents. It does not by itself restrain creatures, deal damage, or create traps.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":89863,"source_global_line_start":89853,"source_heading":"Base Ability - Spool and Strand","source_local_line_end":83,"source_local_line_start":73,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Special Trigger","canonical_action_type":"Special Trigger","cost":"None for mundane thread; 1 CP to create or reinforce Qi Thread for combat use.","factory_combat_bucket":"passive","factory_routing":"triggered_passive_modifier_row","range":"Self.","timing_detail":"No action for ordinary handling; part of the action for Thread talents"}},{"component_name":"Draw the Line","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Base Ability - Draw the Line
Action Type: Multi-Mode
Canonical Action Type: Multi-Mode
Factory Combat Bucket: action
Timing Detail: Action, or replace one attack when you take the Attack action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode
Split Review Decision: same_bucket_attack_replacement_mode
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ACTION_DRAW_THE_LINE->action, ATTACK_REPLACEMENT_DRAW_THE_LINE->action
Range: Mundane 20 feet, Qi Thread 30 feet.
Cost: None for mundane thread if you have thread stock; 1 CP for Qi Thread or to ignore mundane stock.
Target: One creature, object, weapon, surface, or unattended item within range.
Effect: Make a Thread Attack. On a hit, you create a Thread Line between yourself or an anchor you control and the target. The line lasts until the end of your next turn. Choose one basic effect.
Pull: Move the target 5 feet toward you or toward the anchor if it is your size or smaller. Larger creatures are not moved unless they fail a Strength saving throw.
Snare: The target’s speed is reduced by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
Guide: The next attack roll you make against the target before the end of your next turn ignores half cover.
Trip: The target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or fall Prone. This option requires the target to be no more than one size larger than you.
Disarm: The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or drop one held object of your choice in its space. This option requires a mundane line, Qi Thread, or needle to reach the object.
Damage: Draw the Line does not deal damage unless you choose Cutting Thread or another talent modifies it.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":89881,"source_global_line_start":89864,"source_heading":"Base Ability - Draw the Line","source_local_line_end":101,"source_local_line_start":84,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Multi-Mode","canonical_action_type":"Multi-Mode","cost":"None for mundane thread if you have thread stock; 1 CP for Qi Thread or to ignore mundane stock.","factory_combat_bucket":"action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row_with_attack_replacement_mode","range":"Mundane 20 feet, Qi Thread 30 feet.","target":"One creature, object, weapon, surface, or unattended item within range.","timing_detail":"Action, or replace one attack when you take the Attack action"}},{"component_name":"Threaded Strike","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Base Ability - Threaded Strike
Action Type: Linked Modifier
Canonical Action Type: Linked Modifier
Factory Combat Bucket: passive
Factory Routing: linked_modifier_row
Split Review Decision: linked_modifier_not_standalone_action
Recommended Factory Realization: modes=ON_HIT_THREADED_STRIKE->passive
Timing Detail: Part of a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike
Range: The attack’s normal reach.
Cost: None.
Effect: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike, you may wrap, hook, guide, or tension a thread as part of the hit. Until the start of your next turn, you gain one of the following benefits against that target.
Follow the Sleeve: You may move 5 feet without provoking Opportunity Attacks from that target.
Tighten the Wrist: The target has disadvantage on the next Opportunity Attack it makes before the start of your next turn.
Draw the Guard: Your next Thread Attack against the target before the end of your next turn has advantage.
Weighted Knot: Add your Proficiency Bonus to the damage of the triggering attack. You can use Weighted Knot only once per round.
Threaded Strike is the common martial face of this sphere. Many Body Refiners learn Thread this way before ever projecting visible Qi Thread.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":89897,"source_global_line_start":89882,"source_heading":"Base Ability - Threaded Strike","source_local_line_end":117,"source_local_line_start":102,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Linked Modifier","canonical_action_type":"Linked Modifier","cost":"None.","factory_combat_bucket":"passive","factory_routing":"linked_modifier_row","range":"The attack’s normal reach.","timing_detail":"Part of a melee weapon attack or Unarmed Strike"}},{"component_name":"Listen Through Tension","exact_source_excerpt":"#### Base Ability - Listen Through Tension
Action Type: Bonus Action
Factory Combat Bucket: bonus_action
Factory Routing: combat_action_row
Range: One active Thread Line you maintain.
Cost: None.
Effect: You read vibration, breath, resistance, and movement through a Thread Line. Until the end of your next turn, choose one benefit against the connected target or object.
You know whether the target is moving closer, farther, or staying still.
You know whether the target is holding the line, cutting the line, or ignoring it.
You have advantage on one Wisdom (Insight), Wisdom (Perception), or Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check involving the line.
If the target is Invisible but physically connected by a mundane or Qi Thread, you know its space until the line ends, though this does not by itself let you see the target.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":89908,"source_global_line_start":89898,"source_heading":"Base Ability - Listen Through Tension","source_local_line_end":128,"source_local_line_start":118,"structured_fields":{"action_type":"Bonus Action","cost":"None.","factory_combat_bucket":"bonus_action","factory_routing":"combat_action_row","range":"One active Thread Line you maintain."}}]

[{"component_name":"Dart Mechanism","exact_source_excerpt":"### Dart Mechanism — Dart Pattern
Construct a spring, wire, blade, needle, bolt, or comparable projectile mechanism.
When triggered, choose one space occupied by the trap as the point of origin. The dart flies in a straight line up to 90 feet in a direction chosen when you set the trap.
The projectile stops at the first solid surface or creature in its path.
If the first creature in the path would be struck, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against that creature.
Hit: Deal Piercing damage.
Dart damage:
CL 1–4: 1d6
CL 5–10: 2d6
CL 11–16: 3d6
CL 17–20: 4d6","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":91102,"source_global_line_start":91092,"source_heading":"Dart Mechanism — Dart Pattern","source_local_line_end":96,"source_local_line_start":86,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Tripwire","exact_source_excerpt":"### Tripwire — Snare Pattern
Stretch wire, rope, thread, or a comparable low obstruction through the trap’s spaces.
When a creature enters one of those spaces for the first time on a turn, it makes a Dexterity saving throw.
Failed Save: The creature has the Prone condition.
Successful Save: The creature avoids the effect and becomes aware of the trap.
Tripwire is not destroyed when triggered.
A creature aware of the Tripwire has Advantage on its saving throw against it.
A creature that already has the Prone condition does not trigger Tripwire.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":91110,"source_global_line_start":91103,"source_heading":"Tripwire — Snare Pattern","source_local_line_end":104,"source_local_line_start":97,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Activation Trap","exact_source_excerpt":"### Activation Trap — Snare Pattern
Rig one ordinary consumable item to activate when the trap is triggered.
Examples include:
Alchemist’s Fire;
Acid;
Ball Bearings;
Caltrops;
dyes;
perfumes;
smoke pellets;
noise-makers;
appropriate ordinary Alchemy or Tinker consumables.
When triggered, the item activates. If the item normally requires a target, target the triggering creature. If the item creates an area, its point of origin is one of the trap’s spaces, chosen when you set the trap.
You may load multiple copies of the same consumable. Each trigger activates only one loaded item. Activation Trap remains armed while at least one loaded item remains.
Unused recoverable items may be removed from a disarmed or expired trap.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":91125,"source_global_line_start":91111,"source_heading":"Activation Trap — Snare Pattern","source_local_line_end":119,"source_local_line_start":105,"structured_fields":{}}]

[{"component_name":"Black Trace","exact_source_excerpt":"### Black Trace
**Action Type:** Action
**Range:** 30 feet
**Target:** One creature or object you can see
**Cost:** None
Make a ranged Cultivation Attack.
On hit, the target takes Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Safe Black Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 1d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 3d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
On hit, choose one Trace effect:
**Fray.** The target cannot regain HP until the start of your next turn.
**Crack.** If the target is an object, construct, armor, shield, barrier, or temporary qi structure, it takes additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
**Sting.** The target cannot take Reactions against you until the start of your next turn.
**Mark.** The next Unmaking talent that damages the target before the end of your next turn deals additional Ruin damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
You may Overdraw when Black Trace hits.
#### Unbound Trace
Before making the Black Trace attack, you may make the Trace unstable.
On hit, the damage becomes the Unbound Trace value instead.
| Realm | Unbound Trace Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Foundation | 4d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Core Formation | 6d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
| Nascent Soul | 8d10 + your Unmaking key ability modifier |
After the attack resolves, whether it hits or misses, choose one:
- gain 1 Black Vein Strain;
- take Ruin self-damage equal to **1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus**;
- one suitable focus, needle, talisman, weapon, or External Channel gains 1 Crack.
You may Overdraw when Unbound Trace hits.

- a held weapon;
- an unarmed strike;
- one hand or limb;
- a talisman, needle, chain, or tool;
- another object the GM agrees can briefly hold Unmaking qi.
The next time before the duration ends that you hit with that Channel, deal additional Ruin damage based on your Realm.
| Realm | Ruin Channel Bonus Damage |
|---|---:|
| Mortal | 2d8 |
| Foundation | 3d8 |
| Core Formation | 5d8 |
| Nascent Soul | 7d8 |

- the Channel gains 1 Crack if it is an External Channel;
- you gain 1 Black Vein Strain if it is an Internal Channel;

This bonus applies only once per creature per turn.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":95603,"source_global_line_start":95601,"source_heading":"Press the Opening Standard","source_local_line_end":114,"source_local_line_start":112,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"Momentum Marks","exact_source_excerpt":"### Momentum Marks
A Momentum Mark represents the pressure gathered when allies follow your command.
You can hold a number of Momentum Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
You gain 1 Momentum Mark the first time on each turn that one of the following happens:
a Commanded ally benefits from your active Standard;
a Commanded ally hits a creature you have verbally or visibly identified as the objective;
a Commanded ally uses the Help action to aid another Commanded ally;

When you first gain the Sphere of Wax, you gain Mold Wax, Press Seal, and Kindle Wax.
You also learn one Wax talent of your choice.
#### Mold Wax
Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration Concentration, up to 1 minute.
You create or awaken cultivated wax in an unoccupied space, on a surface, or over an unattended object within range. Choose one form.
Soft Spread. You create a 10-foot square of Soft Wax on a surface. The area is Difficult Terrain for hostile creatures. The first hostile creature each round that enters the area or starts its turn there must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or become impressed by the wax until the end of your next turn.
Set Shape. You create a Set Wax panel, ramp, handhold, brace, small bridge, shield plate, low wall, or similar structure that fits within two contiguous 5-foot cubes. It must be supported by a surface unless a talent says otherwise. It can provide cover, block a narrow passage, support weight, or create a short ramp or platform.
Fine Work. Outside initiative, you can shape wax into seals, molds, masks, tablets, candle forms, practice tools, ritual counters, labels, evidence casts, and small sculptures. Fine Work cannot create valuable trade goods, magical items, living organs, or permanent infrastructure unless the GM says otherwise.
At CL 5, your Soft Spread can cover a 15-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within four contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 10, your Soft Spread can cover a 20-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within six contiguous 5-foot cubes.
At CL 15, your Soft Spread can cover a 25-foot square, or your Set Shape can fit within eight contiguous 5-foot cubes.
#### Press Seal
Action. Range 30 feet. Cost 1 CP. Duration 1 minute.
You press or throw a cultivated Wax Seal onto one creature, object, surface, or 5-foot space within range. A willing creature, unattended object, or surface is sealed automatically. An unwilling creature or attended object makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, the seal attaches. On a success, the seal fails.
When you place the seal, choose one base seal.
Clinging Seal. The sealed creature’s Speed is reduced by 10 feet while the seal remains. If placed on an object, the object adheres to the surface it touches and requires an Action and a successful Strength check against your Cultivation Save DC to remove.
Witness Seal. The seal records the next creature other than you that touches, opens, damages, moves, or passes through the sealed target. You know that the seal was triggered if you are within 1 mile, and you can later inspect the seal to see the outline, handprint, footprint, tool mark, weapon shape, or other physical Impression left behind.
Closing Seal. The seal holds a door, lid, drawer, container, wound wrapping, sheath, scroll case, coffin, or similar closure shut. Opening it requires an Action and a successful Strength check or Dexterity check with appropriate tools against your Cultivation Save DC. A creature can also destroy the seal normally.
Preserving Seal. The sealed object, corpse, medicine, food, blood sample, written page, track, footprint, wound dressing, or physical clue resists decay, contamination, smearing, and ordinary weather while the seal remains.
#### Kindle Wax
Bonus Action. Range 60 feet. Cost 0 CP.
You burn one Wax form, Wax Seal, candle, or wax object you created within range. The chosen wax is consumed. Choose one base release.
Candleflare. One creature within 5 feet of the kindled wax makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, it takes fire damage equal to 1d6 + your Proficiency Bonus. On a success, it takes half damage.
Smoke Puff. The wax releases thick smoke in a 5-foot radius until the start of your next turn. The area is Lightly Obscured. This smoke is ordinary smoke once released and can be dispersed by strong wind.
Release Seal. If the kindled wax was a Wax Seal on an ally, the ally gains temporary hit points equal to your Proficiency Bonus. If it was a Wax Seal on an enemy, that enemy takes fire damage equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Mark the Wick. You learn whether the wax had been touched, moved, damaged, or disturbed since you created it. Force the Rising. | Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |

It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.","match_kind":"source_heading","source_global_line_end":102248,"source_global_line_start":102237,"source_heading":"Applying a Rising Mark","source_local_line_end":66,"source_local_line_start":55,"structured_fields":{}},{"component_name":"BASE SPHERE ABILITIES","exact_source_excerpt":"### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yang sphere uses Rising Marks. A Rising Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Rising Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark represents a motion, wound, breath, oath, technique, or intention that has begun to swell toward completion.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Rising Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature, object, or ongoing effect can have only one Rising Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Rising Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked subject is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Kindled and Overkindled Marks
A Rising Mark has one of two expressions.
Kindled Mark. A Rising Mark on you, a willing creature, an unattended object, or an effect you created is a Kindled Mark. You spend Kindled Marks to help an action complete.
Overkindled Mark. A Rising Mark on an unwilling creature, hostile object, enemy effect, or creature that rejects your assistance is an Overkindled Mark. You spend Overkindled Marks to make hostile exertion overcomplete, exposing or straining the source.
A willing creature may end your Rising Mark on itself at any time, no Action required.
#### Applying a Rising Mark
You can apply a Rising Mark in three basic ways.
Kindle the Rising. As a Bonus Action, choose yourself or one willing creature, unattended object, or ongoing effect you created within 60 feet that you can perceive. The target gains one Kindled Mark.
Force the Rising. As a Reaction when a creature, object, or effect within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, uses a limited feature, teleports, becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Overkindled Mark to the source after the triggering event resolves.
Rising Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Fire, Radiant, or Force damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Overkindled Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Rising Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi becoming too bright, too hot, or too forceful to remain unfinished.
#### Spending a Rising Mark
Once per round, when a marked subject you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Rising Mark without using an Action. Choose one Completing Response appropriate to the mark.
#### Kindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend a Kindled Mark.
Complete Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage. Add 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier to one damage roll. This bonus increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Complete Aim.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Add 1d4 to the attack roll, or choose one target making the saving throw and subtract 1d4 from that saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Step.
Trigger: the marked subject begins movement during its turn. Increase one of the subject’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or allow it to stand from Prone without spending movement. At CL 11, the Speed increase becomes 20 feet.
Complete Breath.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points or gains Temporary HP. Increase the amount gained by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier.
Complete Resolve.
Trigger: the marked subject makes a saving throw against an effect that would reduce its Speed, prevent it from taking Reactions, impose Frightened, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious, or suppress its ability to act. Add 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the die becomes 1d6.
Complete Revelation.
Trigger: the marked subject makes an attack roll, Wisdom (Perception) check, or Intelligence (Investigation) check against a creature or effect that is Hidden, Invisible, heavily obscured, disguised by illusion, or concealed by a Yin-like technique. The marked subject ignores Disadvantage from not seeing the target for that roll, provided it can still identify the target’s space or general location.
#### Overkindled Responses
You may use these responses when you spend an Overkindled Mark.
Overheat Force.
Trigger: the marked subject deals damage, makes an attack roll, or forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. After the triggering act resolves, the subject takes Fire or Radiant damage equal to 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This damage increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
Overexpose.
Trigger: the marked subject becomes Hidden, becomes Invisible, creates concealment, creates an illusion, or benefits from a feature that prevents others from perceiving it. Until the start of your next turn, the subject cannot benefit from being Hidden or Invisible against you, and allies you choose within 60 feet know the subject’s current space if they can perceive the area.
Overcommit Step.
Trigger: the marked subject moves at least 10 feet, teleports, or uses special movement. After the movement resolves, the subject cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn. If the movement was teleportation and the destination is within 120 feet of you, you know the destination space.
Overgrown Recovery.
Trigger: the marked subject regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Until the start of your next turn, the first damage roll against that subject gains a bonus equal to your Proficiency Bonus.
Overstrain Technique.
Trigger: the marked subject spends CP, uses a spell slot, activates a limited feature, or uses a named cultivation technique. If the subject uses the same named spell, sphere talent, forged technique, monster action, or cultivation ability again before the end of its next turn, it gains a Rising Mark immediately after the repeated ability resolves.
#### Yang Saves
Some Yang features require a saving throw. [{"component_name":"BASE SPHERE ABILITIES","exact_source_excerpt":"### BASE SPHERE ABILITIES
The Yin sphere uses Waning Marks. A Waning Mark is not a condition. Immunity to a condition does not grant immunity to Waning Marks unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark represents a motion, technique, wound, breath, or intention that has begun to decline before it finishes expressing itself.
#### Mark Limit
You can maintain a number of Waning Marks equal to your Proficiency Bonus. A creature can have only one Waning Mark from you at a time unless a feature says otherwise.
A Waning Mark lasts until the end of your next turn, until you spend it, or until the marked creature is no longer on the same plane of existence as you.
#### Marking a Creature
You can apply a Waning Mark in three basic ways.
Mark the Waning. As a Bonus Action, choose one creature within 60 feet that you can see, hear, or otherwise perceive clearly. The target gains one Waning Mark.
Receive Overextension. As a Reaction when a creature within 60 feet that you can perceive hits with an attack, forces a saving throw, regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, spends CP, uses a spell slot, teleports, or moves at least 10 feet during its turn, you may apply one Waning Mark to that creature after the triggering event resolves.
Withdrawing Thread. As an Action, make a ranged Cultivation Attack against one creature or object within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes Cold or Necrotic damage, chosen when you make the attack, and gains one Waning Mark.
| Cultivation Level | Withdrawing Thread Damage |
| --- | --- |
| CL 1-4 | 1d6 |
| CL 5-10 | 2d6 |
| CL 11-16 | 3d6 |
| CL 17-20 | 4d6 |
The damage is not the sphere’s identity. It is the visible symptom of qi cooling as the target’s action begins to wane.
#### Spending a Waning Mark
Once per round, when a marked creature you can perceive performs a triggering act, you may spend its Waning Mark without using an Action. Choose one Diminishing Response appropriate to the trigger.
**Diminish Force**
Trigger: the marked creature deals damage. Reduce one damage roll by 1d6 + your Key Ability modifier. This reduction increases to 2d6 at CL 5, 3d6 at CL 11, and 4d6 at CL 17.
**Diminish Aim**
Trigger: the marked creature makes an attack roll. Subtract 1d4 from the attack roll. At CL 11, subtract 1d6 instead.
**Diminish Power**
Trigger: the marked creature forces one or more creatures to make a saving throw. Choose one creature making that saving throw. The chosen creature adds 1d4 to the saving throw. At CL 11, the bonus becomes 1d6.
**Diminish Step**
Trigger: the marked creature begins movement, including teleportation. Reduce one of the creature’s Speeds by 10 feet until the end of the current turn, or reduce the distance of one teleportation effect by 10 feet. At CL 11, the reduction becomes 20 feet.
**Diminish Recovery**
Trigger: the marked creature regains Hit Points, gains Temporary HP, restores CP, or benefits from regeneration. Reduce the amount gained or restored by your Proficiency Bonus + your Key Ability modifier, to a minimum of 0.
**Diminish Readiness**
Trigger: the marked creature takes a Reaction or would gain Advantage on a roll. The creature cannot take Reactions until the start of its next turn, or the triggering Advantage is canceled for that roll.
#### Yin Saves
Some Yin features require a saving throw. Unless a feature says otherwise, your Cultivation Save DC equals your Cultivation Save DC.
#### Marked Allies
You may place a Waning Mark on a willing ally. When you do, the mark represents preservation rather than harm. You may spend that mark only for Diminish Force, Diminish Power, Diminish Step, or Diminish Recovery if doing so benefits the ally.
